# About this booklet

Northwind Life & Health provides the Group Extended Health and Dental, Class A plan described in this booklet. Coverage is effective January 1, 2025 under a group policy issued in Ontario. The benefit year runs from January 1 to December 31, and all amounts are in Canadian dollars.

This booklet is a summary. The group policy held by your employer is the legal contract and governs if there is any difference between this booklet and the policy. Words explained in the Definitions section on page 12 have a specific meaning.

# Extended health care

## Paramedical practitioners

The plan pays for treatment by the practitioners listed below when the practitioner is licensed or registered with the regulatory body in the province where the service is provided, and the treatment is within their scope of practice. A physician's referral is not required.

- Massage therapy (registered massage therapist): 80% up to $80 per visit, to a maximum of $500 per person per benefit year. Treatment must be provided by a registered massage therapist; services by other massage practitioners are not eligible.
- Physiotherapy: 80%, to a maximum of $750 per person per benefit year.
- Chiropractor: 80% up to $60 per visit, to a maximum of $500 per person per benefit year.
- Naturopath: 80%, to a maximum of $300 per person per benefit year. Remedies and supplements are not covered.

### What is not covered

- Missed or cancelled appointment fees, and charges for completing forms or reports
- Treatment by a practitioner who is a member of your immediate family
- Services provided at a spa, gym or fitness facility, or for recreational or sports purposes
- Assessments required by an employer, a school, another insurer or for legal proceedings

### Direct billing

Many clinics can bill the plan directly. You pay only the part of the fee that the plan does not cover, and the amount the plan pays still counts toward your maximums.

### Receipts for paramedical claims

Receipts must show the practitioner's full name, professional designation and registration number, the patient's name, the date of each treatment and the amount charged for each visit.

Speech therapy, osteopathy and podiatry

These practitioners are not covered under Class A. Some of their services may be eligible under your health spending account, described on page 12.

# Mental health and the combined maximum

## Mental health practitioners

Psychologists, registered psychotherapists and social workers (MSW): 100%, to a combined maximum of $1,500 per person per benefit year. The practitioner must be a psychologist, registered psychotherapist or master's-level social worker. These services are not part of the paramedical combined maximum.

Sessions may be in person or by secure video. Couples and family counselling sessions are eligible and are claimed under the name of one covered person.

## Paramedical combined maximum

Massage therapy, physiotherapy, chiropractic and naturopathy share a combined maximum of $1,500 per person per benefit year. Each practitioner's individual maximum still applies within the combined maximum.

Example

In one benefit year the plan reimburses $500 for a person's massage therapy and $600 for their physiotherapy. That uses $1,100 of the combined maximum, so $400 remains for chiropractic, naturopathy or further physiotherapy. Physiotherapy is limited to a further $150 by its own maximum.

### Finding a practitioner

Use the provider search in your online account to find psychologists, registered psychotherapists and social workers near you, including practitioners who offer sessions in French or by video. Receipts must show the practitioner's designation and registration number, the length of the session and the fee.

## Employee and family assistance program

Confidential short-term counselling is also available at no cost through your employer's employee and family assistance program. Sessions through the program are not claimed under this plan and do not reduce your maximums. Call 1-800-555-0163 at any time of day.

## Crisis support

If you or someone you know is in immediate danger, call 911 or go to the nearest emergency department. You can also call or text 988, the suicide crisis helpline, at any time.

# Vision care

Vision care benefits help with the cost of routine eye examinations and prescription eyewear for you and your covered dependants.

## Eye exam

Eye examinations: 100% up to $100, one exam every 24 months per person.

## Glasses and contact lenses

Prescription glasses, contact lenses or laser eye surgery: 100%, to a maximum of $300 per person in any 2 consecutive benefit years. Glasses and contact lenses must be prescribed by an optometrist or ophthalmologist. Laser eye surgery counts toward this maximum.

### How the 2-year eyewear maximum works

The $300 maximum is shared across any 2 benefit years in a row. For example, if the plan pays $220 for a person's glasses in 2025, up to $80 is available for their eyewear or laser eye surgery for the rest of 2025 and for 2026.

### Not covered

- Sunglasses, safety glasses and non-prescription lenses
- Replacement of lost or broken eyewear beyond the maximum
- Lens cleaning products, cases and extended warranties
- Vision therapy, orthoptic training and visual training aids

Example

An eye exam costs $120. The plan pays $100, and the remaining $20 can be claimed from your health spending account.

### Eyewear receipts

Receipts for glasses or contact lenses must show the name of the prescribing optometrist or ophthalmologist, the date of the prescription, and the cost of frames and lenses listed separately.

Tip

Ask your optometrist for an itemized receipt that lists the eye exam and each eyewear item separately, with the date of the prescription.

# Prescription drugs

Eligible prescription drugs are reimbursed at 80% after the annual deductible. To be eligible, a drug must require a prescription and have a drug identification number (DIN).

Annual deductible: $25 per family per benefit year, applied to prescription drugs only.

## Your pay-direct drug card

Show your pay-direct drug card at the pharmacy and the plan pays its share directly. You pay the deductible and the remaining 20% at the counter. If you do not have your card with you, pay the pharmacy and submit a claim with the receipt.

Example

The first prescription of the benefit year costs $60, including the dispensing fee. The first $25 is the family deductible, and the plan pays 80% of the remaining $35, which is $28.

### Generic substitution

Generic substitution applies: when a lower-cost generic equivalent is available, reimbursement is based on the price of the lowest-cost generic drug, unless a medical reason for the brand-name drug is approved in advance.

### Drugs that are not covered

- Vitamins, minerals and nutritional supplements, even when prescribed
- Drugs used for cosmetic purposes or for weight loss
- Fertility drugs and drugs for erectile dysfunction
- Products that do not legally require a prescription
- Drugs that a provincial government drug plan pays for

Government drug plans

If you or a dependant is eligible for a provincial drug program, that program pays first and this plan considers the remaining balance.

# Medical supplies, hospital and travel

## Medical supplies and equipment

The following supplies, equipment and hospital services are covered when they are medically necessary and provided by a recognized supplier or hospital.

- Custom-made foot orthotics: 80%, one pair to a maximum of $400 per person every 24 months. A prescription from a physician or podiatrist is required, and the receipt must confirm gait analysis and casting.
- Surgical compression stockings: 80%, up to 2 pairs per person per benefit year. A prescription from a physician is required.
- Semi-private hospital room: 100% of the difference between ward and semi-private accommodation, no maximum. Coverage is for a semi-private room in a Canadian hospital. Private rooms, telephone and television charges are not covered.

## Emergency travel medical

### Emergency out-of-province medical

Emergency medical treatment outside your province: 100%, to a maximum of $5,000,000 per trip, for trips of up to 60 days. Coverage applies only to trips of 60 days or less. You, or someone on your behalf, must call the assistance line within 24 hours of admission to hospital.

Before you travel

Carry your travel assistance card. Emergency travel coverage is for a sudden and unforeseen illness or injury. It does not pay for treatment you travel to receive, or for care that could reasonably wait until you return home. Assistance line: 1-800-555-0177.

### Supplies and travel expenses that are not covered

- Off-the-shelf arch supports, footwear and shoe modifications
- Exercise equipment, air conditioners, humidifiers and whirlpool baths
- Travel expenses for a trip taken against medical advice, or after a diagnosis of a terminal illness
- Treatment of a medical condition that was not stable in the 90 days before your departure
- Follow-up care after you are medically fit to return to your home province

# Dental care

Dental benefits are reimbursed up to the current Ontario Dental Association fee guide for general practitioners, which sets the maximum eligible fee for each procedure. If your dentist charges more than the fee guide, you pay the difference.

Dental annual maximum: $2,000 per person per benefit year for all dental services combined.

## Basic dental services

Basic services, including fillings, extractions, x-rays, endodontics and periodontics: 80%. Endodontics includes root canal therapy; periodontics includes treatment of the gums and the tissues that support the teeth.

### Common procedure codes

| Code | Procedure | Service type | Plan pays |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 01202 | Recall examination | Recall | 90% |
| 11101 | Scaling, first unit of time | Recall | 90% |
| 11111 | Polishing | Recall | 90% |
| 02111 | Periapical radiograph, single image | Basic | 80% |
| 21211 | Amalgam filling, one surface, permanent tooth | Basic | 80% |
| 71101 | Extraction, erupted tooth, single | Basic | 80% |
| 27201 | Crown, porcelain fused to metal | Major | 50% |
| 62501 | Bridge pontic, porcelain fused to metal | Major | 50% |

Codes are shown for reference only. Your dentist's claim may use different codes for similar procedures.

Which fee guide applies?

If you receive dental treatment outside Ontario, the fee guide for general practitioners in the province where the treatment is provided applies.

# Dental care, continued

## Recall exams and cleanings

Recall examinations and cleanings: 90%, once every 9 months per person. Recall services include recall examinations, scaling and polishing.

## Major restorative dental

Major restorative services (crowns, bridges and dentures): 50%, after 12 months of continuous coverage. The 12-month waiting period is counted from the member's coverage start date. Predetermination is recommended for treatment over $500.

## Predetermination

Before starting extensive treatment, ask your dentist to send a treatment plan to Northwind Life & Health. We will tell you how much the plan will pay so you can plan for your share of the cost. A predetermination is valid for 90 days.

### Dental services that are not covered

- Orthodontic treatment, including braces and clear aligners
- Dental implants and related surgery
- Cosmetic procedures such as whitening and veneers
- Replacement of lost or stolen dentures
- Charges for appointments that are missed or cancelled

Example

A crown has an eligible fee of $1,100 under the fee guide. After 12 months of continuous coverage the plan pays 50%, which is $550, and that amount counts toward the dental annual maximum.

Keeping track of your dental maximum

Recall, basic and major services all count toward the same dental annual maximum. You can check your remaining balance online at any time.

# Health spending account

Your employer credits $500 to your health spending account at the start of each benefit year. Unused credits carry forward for 1 benefit year; credits still unused at the end of that year are forfeited.

You can use your health spending account for health and dental expenses that qualify as medical expenses under the Income Tax Act (Canada), including the part of a claim that this plan does not pay. Claims are paid from the account up to the available balance.

When you submit an extended health care or dental claim, any amount the plan does not reimburse is paid from your health spending account automatically, unless you opt out online.

- Eligible expenses include dental and vision costs above your plan maximums, deductibles and prescribed medical devices
- Submit health spending account claims online, at the same time as your regular claims
- Your current balance is shown in your online account

# Definitions

- Benefit year: the 12-month period from January 1 to December 31.
- Consecutive benefit years: benefit years that follow one another without a gap.
- Dependent child: your or your spouse's unmarried child who is under age 21, or under age 25 if a full-time student, or of any age if disabled and dependent on you for support.
- Pay-direct: a claim the provider submits electronically so that the plan pays the provider directly.
- Predetermination: an estimate of benefits requested before treatment begins.
- Reasonable and customary: the usual charge for a service or supply in the area where it is provided, as determined by Northwind Life & Health.
- Spouse: the person you are legally married to, or have lived with in a conjugal relationship for at least 12 months.

# Making a claim

## How to submit a claim

- Online or in the app: sign in at myplan.northwind-health.example, choose Submit a claim and upload clear photos of your receipts.
- At your provider: many pharmacies, dental offices and paramedical clinics can submit claims electronically for you.
- By mail: complete a claim form and mail it with your receipts to the address on page 3.

Include your certificate number [CERT_1] and group policy number [POLICY_1] on every claim form.

## Claim deadline

Claims must be received no later than 90 days after the end of the benefit year in which the expense was incurred. Claims received after this deadline will not be paid. If your coverage ends, claims must be received within 90 days after the date your coverage ends.

## Receipts

Every claim must be supported by an itemized receipt. Keep original receipts for 12 months in case of audit. Credit card slips and cash register receipts that do not show the service provided are not accepted.

## Coordination of benefits

If you and your spouse are covered by more than one group plan, the plans work together so that the total paid is not more than the eligible expense. If your spouse has their own plan, claim for your spouse under their plan first. Always claim for yourself under this plan first.

For dependent children, claim first under the plan of the parent whose birthday falls earlier in the calendar year, then send the unpaid balance to the other plan with a copy of the first plan's explanation of benefits.

Direct deposit

Sign up for direct deposit online to receive claim payments faster. Payments are made in Canadian dollars.

### Claim checklist

- The patient's name, exactly as it appears on your coverage certificate
- The provider's name, designation and registration number
- The date and the amount charged for each service
- Proof of payment, such as a paid-in-full receipt
- For drugs, the DIN, quantity and prescription number

# General provisions

## General exclusions

In addition to the exclusions listed with each benefit, the plan does not pay for:

- Services or supplies that are not medically necessary, or that are experimental or investigational
- Expenses that a government health plan pays, or would pay if you were registered with it
- Treatment of injuries that result from war, riot or taking part in a criminal act
- Charges that would not be made if this coverage did not exist
- Expenses incurred before your coverage starts or after it ends

## When coverage ends

Your coverage ends on the earliest of the date your employment ends, the date you retire, the date you are no longer in an eligible class, or the date the group policy ends. Coverage for a dependant ends when your coverage ends or when that person no longer meets the definition of a dependant.

## Your privacy

Northwind Life & Health collects, uses and discloses your personal information to administer the plan, assess claims and meet legal requirements. You can ask to see the personal information in your file by calling customer care.

## Legal actions

Every action or proceeding against an insurer for the recovery of insurance money payable under the contract is absolutely barred unless commenced within the time set out in the Insurance Act (for actions or proceedings governed by the laws of Ontario, the Limitations Act, 2002).

## Questions

Call customer care at 1-800-555-0142, Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Eastern time.
